text:
sarah-support: Hi team — customer (Acme Corp) says CSV export from Console analytics is either empty or truncated for large date ranges. They hit Export > CSV, browser downloads a 0-byte file or a file that drops after ~2000 rows. Job ID: job_2026_03_16_1432. Repro steps included below.

maria-customer: confirming on Chrome (mac) — file saved as export.csv but when opened shows only header row, size 0 or 1.5 KB for the partial case. Tried incognito, same. :confused:

devon-analytics: thanks — can you paste the exact parameters (date range, segmentation)? also did they select gzip option in UI?

sarah-support: date range: 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-15, segmentation: product_id. They didn't toggle any advanced options. Export button shows progress spinner then browser save dialog. No client-side errors in console.

alex-engineer: checking the export job now. I fetched the presigned URL that the server generated for job_2026_03_16_1432. Quick debug notes:
```
# download via curl
curl -v -L -o out.csv "https://presigned-exports.redwood.s3.amazonaws.com/abc123?X-Amz-..."
# HEAD shows:
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# content-encoding: gzip
# content-disposition: attachment; filename=export.csv
# content-length: 1734
```
But when piping through curl the file looks truncated and gunzip fails in many cases.

kevin-ops: @alex-engineer could this be a middleware double-gzip or missing content-encoding on intermediate object? we recently changed the export worker to gzip on upload.

alex-engineer: exactly — root cause appears to be that the object in S3 is stored uncompressed, but our upload flow sets Content-Encoding: gzip incorrectly (or vice versa). Some browsers honor Content-Encoding and try to decompress client-side; when the bytes don't match, you get empty/truncated output. Also some CDNs/proxies strip content-length leading to partial downloads.

devon-analytics: did you find a reproducible curl sequence we can share with the customer?

alex-engineer: yes — reproducer for engineers/customers:
```
# get presigned url from server side (saved earlier)
PRESIGNED_URL="https://presigned-exports.redwood.s3.amazonaws.com/abc123?X-Amz-..."
# try direct download
curl -sS -D - -o out.raw "$PRESIGNED_URL" | tail -n +1
file out.raw
# if content-encoding is gzip but body not gzipped -> out.raw looks like small text (errors) or 0 bytes
# workaround: fetch underlying s3 object via aws cli if you have permissions
aws s3 cp "s3://redwood-exports/exports/job_2026_03_16_1432/export.csv.gz" ./export.csv.gz
gunzip export.csv.gz
```

maria-customer: we don't have aws access. any quick workaround from Console?

sarah-support: asked them to retry Export with a narrower date window as temporary workaround — smaller files succeed. Also suggested try Firefox — it returned the full CSV for one attempt.

kevin-ops: creating internal issue and rollback candidate. @deploy-bot please tag the last export-worker deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T14:00Z export-worker v2.14.3 applied to exports-prod (release-id: r-exports-2143).

alex-engineer: next steps I recommend: 1) Patch export worker to preserve gzip header semantics (do not set Content-Encoding unless body is actually gzipped). 2) Ensure uploader sets Content-Length or uses chunked transfer consistently. 3) Replay failed job artifacts to regenerate proper objects for affected job IDs.

devon-analytics: I'm going to run a quick scan for other jobs that used that deploy between 14:00-14:10Z and flag any with content-encoding mismatches.

kevin-ops: ticket created: SUP-12345 (internal) — assigning to eng-platform. I've queued a replay for job_2026_03_16_1432.

alex-engineer: once replayed we'll update customer and provide a direct download link. leaving note: probable root cause = header/body mismatch from export-worker change in v2.14.3.

sarah-support: thanks all. I'll update the customer with the workaround and ticket number. Closing here when replay completes. :thumbsup:
